title: Participles
objectives: Form and recognize present active participles
Form and recognize perfect passive participles
Form and recognize future active participles
Use participles to express time relationships

vocabulary.definition: about to love, intending to love

grammar.explanation: Participles are verbal adjectives. They have tense (relative time to main verb) and voice. Present participle = action simultaneous with main verb; perfect participle = action prior; future participle = action subsequent or intended.
rules: Participle agrees with noun it modifies in gender, number, case
Present = same time as main verb
Perfect = action completed before main verb
Future = action subsequent to or intended after main verb
Latin has no present passive or perfect active participle

exercises.question: Translate: Milites victores urbem intrant.
exercises.answer: The conquering soldiers enter the city. / The soldiers, having conquered, enter the city.
hints: victores = nom pl of victor (substantive participle)

exercises.question: Analyze: 'Caesar haec dicens milites hortabatur'
exercises.answer: Saying these things, Caesar was encouraging the soldiers. (dicens = simultaneous with hortabatur)

readingPassage.latin: Hannibal, Alpes transgressus, in Italiam venit. Milites fessi sed victores erant. Romani, periculo cognito, exercitum paraverunt. Hannibal, Romam capturus, versus urbem processit.
readingPassage.translation: Hannibal, having crossed the Alps, came into Italy. The soldiers were tired but victorious. The Romans, the danger having been learned, prepared an army. Hannibal, about to capture Rome, advanced toward the city.
